title: Fireworks sales ban and Vision Zero safety upgrades
subtitle: Also covered: procedure by-law rewrite, new East Avenue pedestrian crossover, and student calls for safer crossing near Cameron Heights.
overview: The committee recommended banning the sale of fireworks in Kitchener from January 2026, with shorter permitted hours and higher administrative penalties for misuse {{vote:m3}}. The recommendation matches one being taken to each municipality in the region. A proposal to have staff plan a move away from city-run fireworks displays toward options such as drone shows was defeated {{vote:m4}}.

The committee also recommended implementing the 2025 Vision Zero safety improvements, including an all-way stop at Fairfield Avenue and St Leger Street and a pedestrian crossover on East Avenue at Borden Street in front of the Kitchener Auditorium {{vote:m2}}. Staff's plan includes a pedestrian refuge island on Stirling Avenue South near Cameron Heights Collegiate, which students asked for.

The committee further recommended replacing Chapter 25 (Procedure) of the Municipal Code {{vote:m1}}. These are recommendations only. Council must adopt them before they take effect. If it does, residents would see changes to fireworks sales and use, and new traffic safety measures on several streets.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended prohibiting fireworks sales from January 2026, tightening the permitted times for setting them off, repealing and replacing Chapter 739, and approving higher administrative penalty fines.
An amendment asking staff to report back on moving away from city-run fireworks displays to alternatives such as drone shows was defeated.
The committee recommended that staff implement the 2025 safety improvements listed in the report and that the Uniform Traffic By-law be amended accordingly.

decisions.item: Fairfield and St Leger all-way stop
decisions.detail: The committee recommended installing an all-way stop at Fairfield Avenue and St Leger Street.
The committee recommended a Level 2, Type B pedestrian crossover on East Avenue at Borden Street, with stopping prohibited near the crossing.
The committee recommended repealing and replacing Chapter 25 (Procedure) of the Municipal Code with the by-law attached to report COR-2025-162.

debate: Student delegates from Cameron Heights described unsafe crossings of Stirling Avenue South, citing fast traffic, heavy volumes at school start and end times, and the lack of a crosswalk. They supported the planned refuge island and asked that a crosswalk be considered as well.

Some councillors asked why students do not use the signalized crossing about a five-minute walk away. They urged the delegates to take the issue to the school board and asked for the school board to share responsibility, for example through staggered start times.

Staff said a pedestrian crossover on Stirling would not meet guidelines because it is too close to an existing signalized crossing. They added that school crossings are normally managed by crossing guards, and that painted lines on the road could cause confusion.

On fireworks, supporters said limiting sales would reduce impulse purchases and align rules across the region. Concerns were that people could still buy fireworks outside the region or online, that enforcement is difficult, and that misuse is already illegal behaviour by a few people.

The mayor said the measure restricts the many who use fireworks responsibly without solving the problem. In support of the failed amendment, one councillor raised environmental harms and argued that the city should set an example. Others wanted fireworks kept as an option for community events while drones are explored.
